tei:div.tei:p: the Name of the Almighty, the King, the Great, the Mighty, the awesome One; holy is He. And they all take upon themselves the yoke of Divine sovereignty one from the other, and give leave to one another to sanctify their Former in a spirit of serenity with clear speech and pleasantness, all exclaim Kedushah in unison and reverently exclaim:

tei:note.tei:p: Despite the attributes we use to describe Him, He remains holy—beyond our conception.
The yoke of Divine Sovereignty is borne willingly and joyfully by each creature as an emblem of his free service to God.—S.R. Hirsch
They take care not to precede one another in their praise of God. On the contrary, each says to the other, “You begin, because you are greater and more worthy than I.”—Avos of R’ Nosson
The clear speech of the angels is the holy tongue (pure Hebrew).—Ya’avetz
